7.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase, e.g. it said the 300 who lapped were the ones who knelt, and changed the shout to 'Make war for the Lord'), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses. V18 and v20 keep the KJV's shout: The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon.

verses.text: Then Jerubbaal, who is Gideon, and all the people that were with him, rose up early, and pitched (set up camp) beside the well of Harod. So the host (army) of the Midianites was on the north side of them, by the hill of Moreh, in the valley.

And the LORD said to Gideon: The people that are with you are too many for Me to give the Midianites into their hands, lest (or else) Israel vaunt (brag about) themselves against Me, saying: My own hand has saved me.

Now therefore go, proclaim (announce) in the ears of the people, saying: Whoever is fearful and afraid, let that person return and depart (leave) early from mount Gilead. And there returned of the people 22,000. And there remained 10,000.

And the LORD said to Gideon: The people are yet (still) too many. Bring them down to the water, and I will try (test) them for you there. And it shall be, that of whom I say to you: This shall go with you, the same shall go with you. And of whomever I say to you: This shall not go with you, the same shall not go.

So Gideon brought down the people to the water. And the LORD said to Gideon: Every one that laps of the water with his tongue, as a dog laps, him you shall set by himself. Likewise (also) every one that bows down upon his knees to drink.
And the number of those who lapped, putting their hand to their mouth, were 300 men. But all the rest of the people bowed down upon their knees to drink water.
And the LORD said to Gideon: By the 300 men that lapped will I save you, and deliver (hand over) the Midianites into your hand. And let all the other people go every man to his place.

So the people took victuals (food) in their hand, and their trumpets. And Gideon sent all the rest of Israel every man to his tent, and retained (kept) those 300 men. And the host (army) of Midian was beneath him in the valley.
And it came to pass the same night, that the LORD said to Gideon: Arise (get up), go down to the host (army). For I have delivered (handed) it into your hand.
But if you fear to go down, go with Phurah your servant down to the host (army).

And you shall hear what they say. And afterward your hands shall be strengthened to go down to the host (army). Then Gideon went down with Phurah his servant to the outside of the armed men that were in the host (army).

And the Midianites and the Amalekites and all the children of the east lay along in the valley like grasshoppers for multitude (great numbers). And their camels were without number, as the sand by the sea side for multitude (great numbers).

And when Gideon was come, look, there was a man that told a dream to his fellow (friend), and said: Look, I dreamed a dream, and lo (look), a cake (round loaf) of barley bread tumbled into the host (army) of Midian, and came to a tent, and smote (struck) it so that it fell, and overturned it, so that the tent lay flat.

And his fellow (friend) answered and said: This is nothing else save (except) the sword of Gideon the son of Joash, a man of Israel. For into his hand God has delivered (handed) Midian, and all the host (army).

And it was so, when Gideon heard the telling of the dream, and the interpretation (meaning) of it, that he worshipped, and returned into the host (army) of Israel, and said: Arise (get up). For the LORD has delivered (handed) into your hand the host (army) of Midian.
And Gideon divided the 300 men into 3 companies (groups). And he put a trumpet in every man's hand, with empty pitchers (jars), and lamps (torches) inside the pitchers (jars).
And Gideon said to them: Look on me, and do likewise (the same). And look, when I come to the outside of the camp, it shall be that, as I do, so shall you do.
When I blow with a trumpet, I and all that are with me, then blow the trumpets also on every side of all the camp, and say: The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon.

So Gideon, and the 100 men that were with him, came to the outside of the camp in the beginning of the middle watch (about midnight). And they had but newly set the watch (the guards had just changed). And they blew the trumpets, and brake (broke) the pitchers (jars) that were in their hands.

And the 3 companies (groups) blew the trumpets, and brake (broke) the pitchers (jars), and held the lamps (torches) in their left hands, and the trumpets in their right hands to blow with. And they cried: The sword of the LORD, and of Gideon.
And they stood every man in his place round about the camp. And all the host (army) ran, and cried, and fled (ran away).

And the 300 blew the trumpets, and the LORD set every man's sword against his fellow (friend), even throughout all the host (army). And the host (army) fled (ran away) to Bethshittah in Zererath, and to the border of Abelmeholah, to Tabbath.
And the men of Israel gathered themselves together out of Naphtali, and out of Asher, and out of all Manasseh, and pursued (chased) after the Midianites.

And Gideon sent messengers throughout all mount Ephraim, saying: Come down against the Midianites, and take before them the waters to Bethbarah and the Jordan. Then all the men of Ephraim gathered themselves together, and took the waters to Bethbarah and the Jordan.

And they took 2 princes (leaders) of the Midianites, Oreb and Zeeb. And they slew (killed) Oreb upon the rock Oreb, and Zeeb they slew (killed) at the winepress of Zeeb. And they pursued (chased) Midian, and brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon on the other side of the Jordan.
